article_title: The Beaverton School District Arts for Learning (A4L) Lessons Project, an Investing in Innovation (i3) Development Grant: Student Impact Findings from Years 1, 2, and 3
citation: Jonathan Nakamoto, Sandy Sobolew-Shubin, Martin Orland. (2015). The Beaverton School District Arts for Learning (A4L) Lessons Project, An Investing in Innovation (i3) Development Grant: Student Impact Findings from Years 1, 2, and 3. WestEd. https://wested.org
title: Arts for Learning (A4L) Lessons: arts-integrated supplemental literacy curriculum with Units and teaching artist Residencies
description: The A4L Lessons Project is a supplemental literacy curriculum integrating reading, writing, and the arts, designed by Young Audiences, Inc. with University of Washington researchers. Its two main elements are Units of instruction delivered by trained classroom teachers, each focused on an art form (theater, visual arts, music, or dance) and built around central texts, and aligned Residencies in which "a trained teaching artist works in collaboration with the classroom teacher during five one-hour sessions." Each Unit comprises 10 to 19 Lessons with suggested instructional time of 13 to 20 hours, and students work in groups and practice public presentations while practicing 21st century skills.
requirements: Units are delivered by a classroom teacher trained by program staff
Residencies require a trained teaching artist collaborating with the classroom teacher
target_learners: students in grades 3, 4, and 5 in regular classrooms
target_learning_goals: literacy and life skills including critical thinking, creative problem solving, and teamwork
examples: Treatment students received two A4L Lessons Units and one teaching artist Residency each school year across 2011-12 through 2013-14
key_sources: Jonathan Nakamoto, Sandy Sobolew-Shubin, Martin Orland. (2015). The Beaverton School District Arts for Learning (A4L) Lessons Project, An Investing in Innovation (i3) Development Grant: Student Impact Findings from Years 1, 2, and 3. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED560945

article_title: Generalizing a Highly Configurable Analytics Pipeline to Replicate and Support Educational Research Across Multiple Domains
citation: Y. Bai, P. Thajchayapong, A. Goel. (2025). Generalizing a Highly Configurable Analytics Pipeline to Replicate and Support Educational Research Across Multiple Domains. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11877
title: A4L Analytics Pipeline
description: The A4L Analytics Pipeline is a component of the Architecture for AI-Augmented Learning that performs statistical analyses on learner interaction data from educational AI assistants. It is "defined as a state machine that runs in a cloud environment" taking "a JSON-formatted analysis configuration payload as input". A data fetch module retrieves specified datasets into a staging area, and an analysis module performs pre-processing, transforms, and analysis, uploading results to durable object storage for the Visualization Pipeline's role-specific dashboards. Daily scheduled runs monitor the published data store for new data and run affected payloads.
requirements: Datasets must be loaded into the A4L published data store by the A4L Data Engine before the pipeline can fetch and analyze them.
An analysis configuration payload specifying dataset, variables, statistic, and result location must be supplied.
constraints: Extension of the pipeline's capabilities in this study was performed by research team members familiar with the system's architecture.
target_learners: graduate-level online computer science students at Georgia Tech
target_learning_goals: understanding AI assistant adoption, performance, need for cognition, and sense of belonging through learning analytics
examples: The pipeline ran Welch's t-tests, contingency tables, and power calculations across the JW, VERA, and SAMI research domains using one codebase.
key_sources: Y. Bai, P. Thajchayapong, A. Goel. (2025). Generalizing a Highly Configurable Analytics Pipeline to Replicate and Support Educational Research Across Multiple Domains. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30303
